metadata.name: Colorado Discretionary Aviation Grant (CDAG)
metadata.agency: Colorado Department of Transportation (CDOT) Division of Aeronautics; Colorado Aeronautical Board
metadata.source_citation: CDOT Aeronautics CDAG program. Managed via WIMS (Web-based Information Management System). Public information: https://www.codot.gov/programs/aeronautics/programs/AviationGrants. Colorado Aeronautical Board approved $9M FY2026 (up from $4.5M FY2025 federal-match grants).

decisions_log.author: APH m49 Sprint 8 reference encoder
decisions_log.decision: Encoded Colorado as additive_100pt model with State/Local + Aviation Education buckets. Detailed scoring criteria are internal (WIMS-managed) and not publicly published.
decisions_log.rationale: CDOT publishes CDAG grant cycles and award totals but not the scoring rubric. Encoded a sensible default framework with 5 buckets covering safety, preservation, federal leverage, capacity/modernization, and system plan alignment. Clear disclaimer that this is a template-style encoding.
decisions_log.source: CDOT Aeronautics public website + general state aviation funding practice

criteria.label: Asset Preservation
criteria.description: Pavement and infrastructure preservation - high priority in Colorado's mountain airport network.

criteria.label: Federal Match Leverage
criteria.description: Colorado prioritizes state matching of federal grants (per CAB's $4.5M FY25 federal-match grant approval).

criteria.label: Modernization / Capacity
criteria.description: Capacity additions, modernization, and capability improvements.

criteria.label: Colorado Aviation System Plan Alignment
criteria.description: Project advances Colorado Aviation System Plan goals.

subcategories.label: Advances CO Aviation System Plan goal
Consistent with current Master Plan / ALP

governance.approval_process: CDOT Aeronautics solicits applications via WIMS. Aeronautical Board approves grant awards (~$9M FY2026, including federal-match and state/local grants).

disclaimer: TEMPLATE-STYLE ENCODING. CDOT manages CDAG scoring internally via WIMS (Web-based Information Management System); the specific scoring rubric is not publicly published. The 5-criterion framework shown here is a reasonable default based on documented program priorities (safety, preservation, federal match) and Aeronautical Board reporting. Colorado stakeholders should obtain the actual WIMS scoring rubric from CDOT Aeronautics (303-512-5250) before adoption or significant decision-making.
